title: WorkerThread is serial host loop
finding: Main host loop waits for next tick, processes cleanup/session input/module entry/status/polling, then timed routines in a fixed serial order.

title: Configurable Timer.Hertz gates idle loop
finding: If Timer.Hertz > 0, AutoResetEvent is set by a timer at 1000/Timer.Hertz ms. WaitForNextTick returns immediately when client input/output/status exists.

title: In-module callback order
finding: For in-module sessions, status STSROU/CYCLE/OUTPUT_BUFFER_EMPTY is processed before CR-terminated STTROU command handling, followed by BEGIN_POLLING if registered.

title: Real-time routine ordering after sessions
finding: After all sessions are processed, host invokes ProcessRTKICK, ProcessRTIHDLR, ProcessSYSCYC, and ProcessTasks in that order.

title: RTKICK delay is seconds-based
finding: RTKICK routines are one-shot delayed callbacks after Delay seconds, executed with channel ushort.MaxValue.

title: RTIHDLR roughly 18 Hz
finding: RTIHDLR routines are described/executed around every 55ms, approximately 18Hz, when registered.

title: SYSCYC after RTIHDLR
finding: SYSCYC module pointer is invoked after RTIHDLR in the timed/real-time phase.

title: BEGIN_POLLING registration
finding: BEGIN_POLLING assigns a per-channel polling routine; STOP_POLLING clears it.

title: Polling routine as often as possible
finding: MBBSEmu comments state BEGIN_POLLING is called as often as possible until STOP_POLLING.

title: TICKER increments once per second
finding: GALGSBL allocates TICKER as ushort and increments it once per second by a Timer callback.

title: Output queued then sent by session sender
finding: SendToClient queues/line-breaks output and can enqueue OUTPUT_BUFFER_EMPTY when buffer drains.

title: Socket sender drains output asynchronously
finding: SendWorker takes DataToClient entries, runs PreSend, heartbeat on idle, and sends queued bytes to socket.

title: Telnet IAC heartbeat is not gameplay tick
finding: Telnet PreSend triggers IAC negotiation every 500ms during early phase, indicating keepalive/negotiation behavior separate from game timing.
